subproblems.title: Covector evaluation bound |α(τ)| ≤ P^n |α| (reused accepted lemma)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every n-covector α on ℝ^P and every τ_1, …, τ_n ∈ ℝ^P with ‖τ_j‖ ≤ 1: |α(τ_1, …, τ_n)| ≤ P^n · covectorEuclideanNorm(α). (Reuse, with identical frozen Lean type, of the comparator-accepted declaration isoperimetric_abs_covector_apply_le.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Eucl P) n) (τ : Fin n → Eucl P), (∀ j, ‖τ j‖ ≤ 1) → |α τ| ≤ (P : ℝ) ^ n * covectorEuclideanNorm α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the accepted proof of the reused declaration isoperimetric_abs_covector_apply_le (node root.isoperimetric-a1.covector_eval_bound-a1), reproduced verbatim; the frozen Lean type is identical, so the comparator-accepted declaration is reused.

Notation. e_a := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ a = EuclideanSpace.single a 1 for a ∈ Fin P; for f : Fin n → Fin P write e_f := (e_{f(1)}, …, e_{f(n)}) and α(e_f) for α applied to this tuple. N(α) := covectorEuclideanNorm α = sqrt(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} (if I is strictly increasing then α(e_I)² else 0)) ≥ 0.

1. Claim: |α(e_f)| ≤ N(α) for every f : Fin n → Fin P.
 (a) If f is not injective, choose i ≠ i' with f(i) = f(i'). The tuple e_f has equal entries in the distinct positions i and i', and α is alternating, so α(e_f) = 0 ≤ N(α) (`ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_eq`).
 (b) If f is injective, let σ := Tuple.sort f, a permutation of Fin n such that f ∘ σ is monotone (`Tuple.monotone_sort`). The map I := f ∘ σ is monotone and injective, hence strictly increasing. Since e_I = e_f ∘ σ and α is alternating, α(e_f ∘ σ) = sign(σ) · α(e_f) (`AlternatingMap.map_perm` applied to α.toAlternatingMap), so |α(e_f)| = |α(e_I)|. As I is strictly increasing, α(e_I)² is one of the nonnegative summands whose sum is N(α)², so α(e_I)² ≤ N(α)² and |α(e_I)| = sqrt(α(e_I)²) ≤ N(α).
2. Expansion. For each j, τ_j = Σ_{a ∈ Fin P} τ_j(a) • e_a (expansion in the standard orthonormal basis). By multilinearity of α (expansion of a multilinear map applied to sums and extraction of scalars: `ContinuousMultilinearMap.map_sum` and `map_smul_univ` applied to α.toContinuousMultilinearMap):
 α(τ_1, …, τ_n) = Σ_{f : Fin n → Fin P} (Π_{j ∈ Fin n} τ_j(f(j))) · α(e_f).
3. For every j and a, |τ_j(a)| ≤ ‖τ_j‖ ≤ 1 (a coordinate of a Euclidean vector is bounded by its norm, `PiLp.norm_apply_le`). Hence |Π_j τ_j(f(j))| = Π_j |τ_j(f(j))| ≤ 1 for every f (a product of numbers in [0, 1], `Finset.prod_le_one₀`).
4. By the triangle inequality and steps 1 and 3, |α(τ_1, …, τ_n)| ≤ Σ_f |Π_j τ_j(f(j))| · |α(e_f)| ≤ Σ_f N(α) = card(Fin n → Fin P) · N(α) = P^n · N(α). (For n = 0 the sum has the single empty f, the product is 1 and the bound reads |α()| ≤ N(α).) ∎
proof_key_steps: |α(e_f)| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α for every f : Fin n → Fin P: zero if f is not injective; otherwise sort f by a permutation σ and use α(e_f ∘ σ) = sign σ · α(e_f).
Expand α(τ) multilinearly in the standard basis: a sum over the P^n maps f of (Π_j τ_j(f j)) α(e_f).
Each coefficient satisfies |Π_j τ_j(f j)| ≤ 1 because |τ_j(a)| ≤ ‖τ_j‖ ≤ 1.

subproblems.title: Mass estimate |T(ω)| ≤ M_W(T)·sup|ω| (reused accepted lemma)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U, W ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n, ω ∈ TestFormOn U n and B, C ∈ ℝ with B ≥ 0, T.massOn W ≤ ofReal B, tsupport ω ⊆ W and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ C for every x. Then |T(ω)| ≤ B·C. (Reuse, with identical frozen Lean type, of the comparator-accepted declaration cmb_abs_apply_le_of_massOn_le.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n) (B C : ℝ), 0 ≤ B → T.massOn W ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B → tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) ⊆ W → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x) ≤ C) → |T ω| ≤ B * C
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the accepted proof of the reused declaration cmb_abs_apply_le_of_massOn_le (node root.compactness_mass_bounds-a1.mass_bound-a1), reproduced verbatim; the frozen Lean type is identical, so the comparator-accepted declaration is reused. It is stated with an explicit real bound B for M_W(T) and an explicit pointwise bound C for |ω|, which avoids dividing by sup|ω| and any case distinction on ω = 0.

Notation: for an n-covector α, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P, I strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)},…,e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2}, where e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i. M_W(T) = T.massOn W is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal(T(ψ)) over ψ ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W = {ψ ∈ TestFormOn U n : tsupport ψ ⊆ W and |ψ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x}.

1. (Homogeneity.) For t ∈ ℝ and a covector α, |tα| = |t|·|α|. Each coefficient satisfies (tα)(e_I) = t·α(e_I), so the sum of squares is multiplied by t², and √(t²S) = |t|·√S.
2. (C ≥ 0.) 0 ≤ |ω(0)| ≤ C.
3. (Admissible rescalings.) Fix a real c > C, so c > 0. Let s ∈ {c⁻¹, −c⁻¹}. TestFormOn U n is a real submodule, so s•ω ∈ TestFormOn U n. Also tsupport(s•ω) ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W, and by Step 1, |(s•ω)(x)| = c⁻¹|ω(x)| ≤ C/c ≤ 1 for every x. Hence s•ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W, and GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn gives ENNReal.ofReal(T(s•ω)) ≤ M_W(T) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B.
4. (Unpacking.) Because B ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal a ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B implies a ≤ B (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff). By linearity T(s•ω) = s·T(ω). Therefore c⁻¹T(ω) ≤ B and −c⁻¹T(ω) ≤ B. Multiplying by c > 0 gives T(ω) ≤ Bc and −T(ω) ≤ Bc, i.e. |T(ω)| ≤ B·c. This holds for every c > C.
5. (Letting c ↓ C.) Let ε > 0 and c := C + ε/(B+1) > C. Step 4 gives |T(ω)| ≤ BC + Bε/(B+1) ≤ BC + ε. Since ε > 0 is arbitrary, |T(ω)| ≤ B·C (le_of_forall_pos_le_add). ∎
proof_key_steps: For c > C, ±c⁻¹ω is mass-admissible for W, so ±c⁻¹T(ω) ≤ B by le_massOn and B ≥ 0.
Hence |T(ω)| ≤ B·c for every c > C; let c decrease to C.

subproblems.title: Coefficient-norm bound for the radial integral
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let ω : ℝ^P → Λ_{m+1}(ℝ^P) be any (m+1)-form (DifferentialForm (Eucl P) (m+1); no regularity is assumed) with covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(y)) ≤ 1 for every y ∈ ℝ^P, let x ∈ ℝ^P, and let β ∈ Λ_m(ℝ^P) be an m-covector with β(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt for every v ∈ (ℝ^P)^m, where (x, v) := Fin.cons x v and the integral is the interval integral over [0, 1]. Then covectorEuclideanNorm(β) ≤ P^{2m+1}·‖x‖.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) (m + 1)) (x : Eucl P) (β : Covector (Eucl P) m), (∀ y, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω y) ≤ 1) → (∀ v : Fin m → Eucl P, β v = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, t ^ m * ω (t • x) (Fin.cons x v)) → covectorEuclideanNorm β ≤ (P : ℝ) ^ (2 * m + 1) * ‖x‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 4 and 5 of the parent proof (coefficient estimate and pointwise bound), stated for an arbitrary covector β given by the radial integral at one point x.
Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α for a covector α on ℝ^P; e_a := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ a for a ∈ Fin P (the standard orthonormal basis, so ‖e_a‖ = 1); for I : Fin m → Fin P, e_I := (e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(m)}); (x, u) := Fin.cons x u. Put K := P^{m+1}‖x‖ ≥ 0.
1. (Coefficient estimate.) Let α ∈ Λ_{m+1}(ℝ^P) and u ∈ (ℝ^P)^m with ‖u_i‖ ≤ 1 for all i. Then |α(x, u)| ≤ P^{m+1}‖x‖·|α|.
 (a) If x = 0, the tuple (x, u) has the zero vector in slot 0, so α(x, u) = 0 by multilinearity (map_coord_zero), and 0 ≤ P^{m+1}·0·|α|.
 (b) If x ≠ 0, then ‖x‖ > 0. Let τ := (‖x‖⁻¹x, u) ∈ (ℝ^P)^{m+1}. Then ‖τ_0‖ = ‖x‖⁻¹‖x‖ = 1 and ‖τ_{i+1}‖ = ‖u_i‖ ≤ 1 for all i. The tuple (x, u) is τ with its slot 0 replaced by ‖x‖·τ_0 (because ‖x‖·(‖x‖⁻¹x) = x), so linearity of α in slot 0 (map_update_smul) gives α(x, u) = ‖x‖·α(τ). The accepted lemma isoperimetric_abs_covector_apply_le (sibling covector_bound, with n := m+1) gives |α(τ)| ≤ P^{m+1}|α|. Hence |α(x, u)| = ‖x‖·|α(τ)| ≤ P^{m+1}‖x‖·|α|.
2. (Each coordinate value of β.) Fix I : Fin m → Fin P and let f(t) := t^m·ω(tx)(x, e_I). For t ∈ Ι(0, 1) = (0, 1] we have 0 ≤ t^m ≤ 1 and |ω(tx)| ≤ 1 by hypothesis, and Step 1 with α := ω(tx) and u := e_I (every ‖e_{I(i)}‖ = 1) gives |ω(tx)(x, e_I)| ≤ P^{m+1}‖x‖·|ω(tx)| ≤ K. Hence |f(t)| ≤ 1·K = K for all t ∈ (0, 1]. By the interval-integral bound ‖∫_a^b f‖ ≤ C·|b − a| whenever ‖f(t)‖ ≤ C for all t ∈ Ι(a, b) (intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const, which needs no integrability hypothesis because the integral of a non-integrable function is 0), |β(e_I)| = |∫_0^1 f(t) dt| ≤ K·|1 − 0| = K. Consequently β(e_I)² = |β(e_I)|² ≤ K².
3. (Summation.) By definition |β| = sqrt(Σ_{I : Fin m → Fin P} s_I), where s_I := β(e_I)² if I is strictly increasing and s_I := 0 otherwise. By Step 2, 0 ≤ s_I ≤ K² for every I, and there are exactly P^m maps I : Fin m → Fin P (Fintype.card_fun). Since sqrt is monotone, |β| ≤ sqrt(P^m·K²). The natural number N := P^m satisfies N ≤ N² (Nat.le_self_pow; N = 0 or N ≥ 1), so P^m·K² ≤ (P^m)²·K² = (P^m·K)² and sqrt(P^m·K²) ≤ sqrt((P^m·K)²) = P^m·K, because P^m·K ≥ 0. Finally P^m·K = P^m·P^{m+1}‖x‖ = P^{2m+1}‖x‖. Hence covectorEuclideanNorm(β) ≤ P^{2m+1}‖x‖. (No case distinction on P is needed: for P = 0 the bound K = 0 forces every term to vanish.) ∎
proof_key_steps: Coefficient estimate |α(x, u)| ≤ P^{m+1}‖x‖·|α| for ‖u_i‖ ≤ 1: zero if x = 0, otherwise α(x, u) = ‖x‖·α(‖x‖⁻¹x, u) and the reused isoperimetric_abs_covector_apply_le.
For every I : Fin m → Fin P, |β(e_I)| ≤ K := P^{m+1}‖x‖ by the constant bound for interval integrals, using 0 ≤ t^m ≤ 1 and |ω(tx)| ≤ 1.
|β|² is a sum over the P^m maps I of terms in [0, K²]; sqrt(P^m K²) ≤ P^m K = P^{2m+1}‖x‖ since P^m ≤ (P^m)².

subproblems.title: Smooth cutoff of the radial form to a bounded test form
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let ω : ℝ^P → Λ_{m+1}(ℝ^P) be any (m+1)-form, let ψ₀ : ℝ^P → Λ_m(ℝ^P) be a C^∞ m-form (ContDiff ℝ ∞) with ψ₀(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt for all x ∈ ℝ^P and v ∈ (ℝ^P)^m ((x, v) := Fin.cons x v), and let 0 < r < s. Then there is a test form ψ ∈ D^m(ℝ^P) = TestFormOn univ m such that (i) ψ(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt for every x in the open ball B_r(0) and every v, and (ii) if covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(y)) ≤ 1 for every y, then covectorEuclideanNorm(ψ(x)) ≤ P^{2m+1}·s for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) (m + 1)) (ψ₀ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) (r s : ℝ), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) ψ₀ → (∀ (x : Eucl P) (v : Fin m → Eucl P), ψ₀ x v = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, t ^ m * ω (t • x) (Fin.cons x v)) → 0 < r → r < s → ∃ ψ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) m, (∀ x ∈ ball (0 : Eucl P) r, ∀ v : Fin m → Eucl P, (ψ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) x v = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, t ^ m * ω (t • x) (Fin.cons x v)) ∧ ((∀ y, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω y) ≤ 1) → ∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ψ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) x) ≤ (P : ℝ) ^ (2 * m + 1) * s)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 0 of the parent proof (ζ_{r,s}ψ_ω is a test form satisfying the radial formula on B_r(0)) and the pointwise part of Step 6 (|ζψ_ω(x)| ≤ c·s), with the smooth radial form ψ_ω supplied as the input ψ₀.
Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; B_ρ(0), B̄_ρ(0) are the open and closed balls; D^m(ℝ^P) := TestFormOn univ m, whose elements are the m-forms f : ℝ^P → Λ_m(ℝ^P) that are C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ∞), have compact support, and satisfy tsupport f ⊆ univ.
1. (Bump function.) Since 0 < r < s and Eucl P is a finite-dimensional inner product space (so it carries smooth bump functions), there is a ContDiffBump ζ centred at 0 with rIn = r and rOut = s. Its coercion ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ is C^∞ (ContDiffBump.contDiff), satisfies 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1 (nonneg, le_one), ζ(x) = 1 for x ∈ B̄_r(0) (one_of_mem_closedBall), support ζ = B_s(0) (support_eq), and has compact support (hasCompactSupport).
2. (The test form.) Define f(x) := ζ(x)·ψ₀(x) ∈ Λ_m(ℝ^P). f is C^∞ as the product of the C^∞ scalar function ζ and the C^∞ form ψ₀ (ContDiff.smul), it has compact support because ζ has (HasCompactSupport.smul_right), and tsupport f ⊆ univ trivially. Hence f ∈ D^m(ℝ^P); let ψ be f regarded as an element of TestFormOn univ m.
3. (Property (i).) Let x ∈ B_r(0) and v ∈ (ℝ^P)^m. Then x ∈ B̄_r(0), so ζ(x) = 1 and ψ(x)(v) = ψ₀(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt by the hypothesis on ψ₀.
4. (Homogeneity.) For a ∈ ℝ and α ∈ Λ_m(ℝ^P): (aα)(e_I) = a·α(e_I) for every coordinate tuple e_I, so the sum of squares S' defining |aα|² equals a² times the sum S defining |α|², and |aα| = sqrt(a²·S) = |a|·sqrt(S) = |a|·|α| (Real.sqrt_mul, Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs).
5. (Property (ii).) Assume |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y and let x ∈ ℝ^P. By Step 4, |ψ(x)| = |ζ(x)|·|ψ₀(x)|.
 (a) If ‖x‖ < s: |ζ(x)| = ζ(x) ≤ 1. The covector β := ψ₀(x) satisfies β(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt for all v, so the sibling lemma iwl_cr_cest_radial_coeff_bound gives |ψ₀(x)| ≤ P^{2m+1}‖x‖. Hence |ψ(x)| ≤ 1·P^{2m+1}‖x‖ ≤ P^{2m+1}·s.
 (b) If ‖x‖ ≥ s: x ∉ B_s(0) = support ζ, so ζ(x) = 0 and |ψ(x)| = 0 ≤ P^{2m+1}·s, as s > r > 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take the ContDiffBump ζ centred at 0 with rIn = r, rOut = s; ψ := ζψ₀ is C^∞ with compact support, i.e. an element of TestFormOn univ m.
ζ = 1 on B̄_r(0) ⊇ B_r(0), so ψ = ψ₀ there and the radial formula holds on B_r(0).
|ψ(x)| = ζ(x)|ψ₀(x)|: for ‖x‖ < s use iwl_cr_cest_radial_coeff_bound and ‖x‖ < s, for ‖x‖ ≥ s ζ(x) = 0; hence |ψ(x)| ≤ P^{2m+1}s.

subproblems.title: Support of a cone over a current supported in a closed ball
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, R ∈ ℝ, X ∈ D_m(ℝ^P) = GeometricCurrentOn univ m and C ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^P) = GeometricCurrentOn univ (m+1) with spt X ⊆ B̄_R(0) and Cone(X, C), i.e. C(ω) = X(ψ) whenever ω ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P), ψ ∈ D^m(ℝ^P) and ψ(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt for all x in some open set N ⊇ spt X and all v ∈ (ℝ^P)^m ((x, v) := Fin.cons x v). Then spt C ⊆ B̄_R(0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (R : ℝ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) m) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) (m + 1)), X.support ⊆ closedBall 0 R → (∀ (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) (m + 1)) (ψ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) m), (∃ N : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen N ∧ X.support ⊆ N ∧ ∀ x ∈ N, ∀ v : Fin m → Eucl P, (ψ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) x v = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, t ^ m * (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) (m + 1)) (t • x) (Fin.cons x v)) → C ω = X ψ) → C.support ⊆ closedBall 0 R
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 2 and 3 of the parent proof. In Step 2 the radius δ of the neighbourhood B_{R+δ}(0) on which ω vanishes is here given explicitly (δ := r), so no compactness or thickening argument is needed.
Notation: D^k(ℝ^P) := TestFormOn univ k. For C ∈ GeometricCurrentOn univ (m+1), spt C = univ ∖ zeroRegion(C), where zeroRegion(C) is the union of all sets W such that W is open, closure W is compact, closure W ⊆ univ, and C vanishes on W, i.e. C(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ W.
1. Let p ∈ spt C and suppose, for contradiction, that p ∉ B̄_R(0), i.e. ‖p‖ > R. Put r := (‖p‖ − R)/2 > 0 and W := B_r(p).
2. W is open; since r ≠ 0, closure W = B̄_r(p) (closure_ball), which is compact (closed balls of the finite-dimensional space ℝ^P are compact), and closure W ⊆ univ.
3. Claim: C vanishes on W. Let ω ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Put N := B_{R+r}(0), an open set; since r > 0, spt X ⊆ B̄_R(0) ⊆ B_{R+r}(0) = N (closedBall_subset_ball). Let x ∈ N, v ∈ (ℝ^P)^m and t ∈ [0, 1]. Then ‖tx‖ = t‖x‖ ≤ ‖x‖ < R + r. If tx belonged to tsupport ω ⊆ B_r(p), then ‖tx − p‖ < r and ‖p‖ ≤ ‖tx‖ + ‖tx − p‖ < (R + r) + r = ‖p‖, which is absurd. Hence tx ∉ tsupport ω, so ω(tx) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and t^m·ω(tx)(x, v) = 0. The integrand therefore vanishes on [0, 1] = uIcc 0 1, and intervalIntegral.integral_congr gives ∫_0^1 t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt = ∫_0^1 0 dt = 0 = 0(x)(v). So ψ := 0 ∈ D^m(ℝ^P) satisfies ψ(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt for all x ∈ N and all v, where N is open and N ⊇ spt X. By Cone(X, C), C(ω) = X(0) = 0, since X is linear.
4. By Steps 2 and 3, W is one of the sets whose union is zeroRegion(C), and p ∈ W because ‖p − p‖ = 0 < r. Thus p ∈ zeroRegion(C), contradicting p ∈ spt C = univ ∖ zeroRegion(C). Hence every p ∈ spt C lies in B̄_R(0), i.e. spt C ⊆ B̄_R(0). (The argument uses no sign condition on R: if R < 0 the same steps apply verbatim.) ∎
proof_key_steps: For p with ‖p‖ > R set r := (‖p‖ − R)/2 > 0 and W := B_r(p), which is open with compact closure B̄_r(p) ⊆ univ.
If tsupport ω ⊆ W, then tx ∉ tsupport ω for x ∈ B_{R+r}(0) and t ∈ [0, 1], so ψ := 0 satisfies the radial formula on the open N := B_{R+r}(0) ⊇ spt X and Cone(X, C) gives C(ω) = X(0) = 0.
Thus W lies in zeroRegion(C) and contains p, contradicting p ∈ spt C; hence spt C ⊆ B̄_R(0).

subproblems.title: Mass comparison through bounded transfer test forms
subproblems.statement: Let P, n, k ∈ ℕ, X ∈ D_n(ℝ^P) = GeometricCurrentOn univ n, C ∈ D_k(ℝ^P) = GeometricCurrentOn univ k and c, R ∈ ℝ with c ≥ 0, R ≥ 0 and M(X) < ∞. Assume that for every ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ k univ (a test k-form with covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(y)) ≤ 1 for all y) and every δ > 0 there is ψ ∈ D^n(ℝ^P) = TestFormOn univ n with C(ω) = X(ψ) and covectorEuclideanNorm(ψ(x)) ≤ c·(R + δ) for all x. Then M(C) ≤ ofReal(c·R)·M(X).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n k : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) n) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) k) (c R : ℝ), 0 ≤ c → 0 ≤ R → X.mass < ∞ → (∀ ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) k univ, ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∃ ψ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) n, C ω = X ψ ∧ ∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ψ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x) ≤ c * (R + δ)) → C.mass ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (c * R) * X.mass
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 6 of the parent proof (the mass bound), with the construction of the transfer forms ψ = ζ_δψ_ω abstracted into the hypothesis.
Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; for T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn univ j, M(T) := T.mass = T.massOn univ = sSup{ofReal(T(ω)) : ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ j univ} ∈ [0, ∞], where ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ j univ means ω ∈ TestFormOn univ j, tsupport ω ⊆ univ and |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.
1. Since M(X) < ∞, B := M(X).toReal ≥ 0 satisfies M(X) = ofReal(B) (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal).
2. Fix ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ k univ. Claim: C(ω) ≤ cR·B. Let ε > 0 and δ := ε/(Bc + 1). As B, c ≥ 0 we have Bc + 1 > 0, δ > 0 and δ(Bc + 1) = ε, hence Bcδ = ε − δ < ε. By hypothesis there is ψ ∈ TestFormOn univ n with C(ω) = X(ψ) and |ψ(x)| ≤ c(R + δ) for all x. Apply the accepted lemma cmb_abs_apply_le_of_massOn_le (sibling mass_bound) with U = W = univ, T = X, the form ψ, the bound B (B ≥ 0 and X.massOn univ = M(X) = ofReal B), tsupport ψ ⊆ univ, and the pointwise bound c(R + δ): |X(ψ)| ≤ B·c(R + δ). Hence C(ω) = X(ψ) ≤ |X(ψ)| ≤ cRB + Bcδ < cRB + ε. As ε > 0 was arbitrary, C(ω) ≤ cRB (le_of_forall_pos_lt_add).
3. By monotonicity of ofReal and since cR ≥ 0: ofReal(C(ω)) ≤ ofReal(cR·B) = ofReal(cR)·ofReal(B) = ofReal(cR)·M(X) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul).
4. M(C) = C.massOn univ is the supremum of ofReal(C(ω)) over ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ k univ, and by Step 3 each of these values is ≤ ofReal(cR)·M(X). Hence M(C) ≤ ofReal(c·R)·M(X) (sSup_le). ∎
proof_key_steps: Write M(X) = ofReal B with B := M(X).toReal ≥ 0.
For admissible ω and δ = ε/(Bc + 1), the hypothesis and cmb_abs_apply_le_of_massOn_le give C(ω) = X(ψ) ≤ Bc(R + δ) < cRB + ε; hence C(ω) ≤ cRB.
ofReal(C(ω)) ≤ ofReal(cR)·ofReal(B) = ofReal(cR)·M(X); taking the supremum over admissible ω gives M(C) ≤ ofReal(cR)·M(X).
